Three moments, not one. Her first answer on your phone is step 3, living with her starts at 6, she becomes someone at 8, you build with her from 9, and your own birth test is 10. A step counts only when you see it on your phone, not on green CI alone.

She stays open. Done when the app stays up with Ollama off and on. Three of four launch fixes are verified, and WAKE-ORDER is tonight.
She's Friday. Scripted rename, CI green. Done when the app name, its id and the code all say Friday. You see steps 1 and 2 together at step 3.
First answer. Install once, Ollama off then on. Done when she answers one message, or the crash log names the next fix. Only the phone can show whether her model name resolves on a real Ollama. We recorded that problem but never fixed it.
A faster builder. One-tap crash export, plus a cloud builder that compiles while it works, so it closes more than one story a night. Unproven: whether the free models answer from cloud runners. One probe settles it, and if they don't, steps 5 to 7 go one at a time.
One Friday on the real path. ONE-2 to ONE-6: one composition, Life Test, recorder, floor, Seed report. Done when the same Friday runs in CI and on your phone, and her model starts with the app with nothing started by hand. The old ONE-3 to ONE-6 work was never verified, so it gets re-earned.
Voice, beside step 5 as soon as step 3 works. Done when you talk for two minutes and interrupt her mid-sentence: English first, then Egyptian, never blocked on a wake word. Her history starts here.
Hands. Open an app, set an alarm, play media, draft a message, each confirmed by the phone's resulting state. The same outcome works by more than one route, and when none works she records a gap.
She changes because of you. You correct her once. After a restart, different wording and the original episode unreachable, she acts differently, a matched control shows why, and the same mechanism works on a second unrelated problem.
She extends herself. She hits something she can't do and names the gap. The builder makes a candidate, it's tested in isolation, approved, adopted and used. From here you build with her.
Birth test. A goal nobody gave a method for. She finds what's missing, gets or builds it, acts, checks the real result, and stays the same individual.

Steps 1 to 3 are the launch chain, 4 sets the pace, 5 to 7 run side by side, and 8 to 10 need them. Each "how" above is today's best guess and can be swapped; each "done when" can't.

The loop logic isn't the problem; what it stands on is. Don't start tonight's run. Do the 10-minute test below first, because it decides what we build.
What the evidence says

Known: zero iterations. In all nine retry rounds, every probe for all three models ran to ralph's own 420 s timeout instead of returning an error. No attempt since about 07:20 on Oct 30 has got through.
Known: it isn't a leftover process (none found at start), your config (same opencode 1.18.20 and settings as the night that worked), or GitHub (reports pushed at 22:11 and 08:11).
Inferred, not proven: the free lane itself. OpenCode's free models are reportedly rate-limited per IP or network and contended, and they're offered "for a limited time". Public reports from late October describe a "free usage exceeded" retry countdown of up to 14 hours, sometimes on the first request of the day. That would also explain the two freezes right after a grep. The test checks this.
My mistake: v4 saved only the last two lines of each failed preflight, which were useless. The real error text is on your phone, and the test collects it.

What I'd do with the process

Dismantle: your phone as the machine that runs the loop, one anonymous free lane as the only brain, and the run-at-night-and-upload ritual.
Keep: stories, red→green proof, CI-honest, ci_verify and the reports branch. They closed two stories honestly.
Build: the same Ralph running in GitHub Actions, which is free for your public repo. Gradle runs in the loop and your phone is only a remote control. Model lanes get a hard no-answer deadline, so a dead lane costs 2 minutes, not 10 hours. Stories get sized by request budget, since free lanes cap volume.
Not doing: paid tiers and local models on the phone.

This is build tooling, not Friday's code. Ralph still writes Friday.
What the test settles

Answers from the cloud, not from your phone: the wall is the free lane on your network, and I move the builder to Actions tonight.
Answers on your phone with the newest client: the old client was the problem, so it's one upgrade command, and we still move to the cloud.

NL=$(ls -t /root/oc_home/.local/share/opencode/log/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -2); if [ -n "$NL" ]; then grep -hiE "free usage|retry|429|403|rate|limit|quota|FreeTier|timed out|timeout|error" $NL 2>/dev/null | tail -20 | cut -c1-260; fi;
else tail -5 "$W/npm.out" | cut -c1-200; fi;

curl -s -X DELETE -H "$HD" "$AP/git/refs/heads/$BR" > /dev/null;
echo "4/4 summary";

echo "--- phone:"; grep -E "^rc=|new client probe|^version|http=|Free usage" "$W/phone.md" | cut -c1-170 | head -14;

Dead lanes cost minutes, not hours: each model must answer a one-word test before the agent gets it. A dead lane costs about 2.5 minutes, then it rotates to the next or waits and retries. It also starts CI builds itself, because the job token's pushes don't trigger them.

rotates the lane when an iteration changes nothing;
stops after about 30 minutes with instructions if no key exists, instead of burning 4 hours.

Your argument, as I understand it

The Builder is scaffolding. It produces the first human Friday, and she absorbs it: it goes from her supervisor to a tool she has.
She starts human-like, not human-limited. The order is first human Friday, then a super-intelligent person, then a hybrid human-machine, and she evolves from the start.
The Builder grows brick by brick, then floor by floor, then building by building. It runs in parallel only once that ability has actually developed.
"Consciousness" in your project means the liquid symbiotic software, not the scientific meaning.
You want the ultimate setup with its tools, and you're tired of Claude and GPT passing the ball.

Where GPT and I land

Took (it rated my runner 6/10, direction and milestones 9/10):
My CI check counted any workflow run, not just the build.
The final step stopped that check before confirming the last build.
The APK release was deleted before the new one existed.
Fixed. A lane must now create a file with a tool, not just answer "ok".


Partly: the agent can see the job token and the NVIDIA key. I dropped the unused OpenRouter key, but the exposure is only reduced, not solved. The real fix is to split a trusted job from an unprivileged agent job. We do that before parallel workers, or before Friday uses the builder herself. The NVIDIA key is free-tier and revocable, so the risk is small for now.
Later (your zero-dollar rule):
Temporal: git state plus relay does this job now.
Kubernetes and microVMs: a runner is already a fresh VM.
LiteLLM: my lane pool covers it until there are more than about 3 providers.
vLLM and GPUs: free keyed lanes until money exists.
OpenHands: keep opencode until the harness, not the models, is what fails.



What changes in the plan

The 10 steps stay. The Builder is a dispatchable workflow with inputs, reports and gates, so Friday absorbing it is a handoff, not a rewrite.
Your "floors" become a rule you can check: two stories in parallel only after 3 cloud runs in a row each close a story with no stall, no auto-reject and no rework.
